title: pxr-effector-uncoupling: cell-type-resolved coupling of PXR (NR1I2) target genes across 446,672 single human cells, with six orthogonal validation layers
description:
Software and data deposit for the manuscript “Cell-type-resolved decoupling of PXR target genes identifies hepatocyte-selective readouts for xenobiotic response” (Shenoy, 2026).

This deposit contains the complete reproducible pipeline, processed data, manuscript text, and rendered figures for an end-to-end analysis of pregnane X receptor (PXR; NR1I2) target-gene coupling across 446,672 single human cells (10 cell types) from CELLxGENE Census v2025-01-30. Six canonical PXR targets — CYP2C9, CYP3A5, ABCC2, SLCO1B1, CYP2C8, and CPT1A — show strong coupling in hepatocytes (Spearman ρ 0.77–0.89, BH q ≈ 0.004) and only weak baseline coupling in immune and placental cells, with a 4–8× effect-size differential.

The result is validated across six orthogonal layers: (i) metacell parameter sweep and 80% cell-level subsampling; (ii) a matched 20-gene negative-control set (PXR-target vs control DS Mann-Whitney U one-sided p = 1.0 × 10−31); (iii) GTEx v8 bulk RNA-seq across 54 tissues; (iv) direct rifamycin perturbation of primary human hepatocytes (GSE139896) confirming four of the six top genes (CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP3A5, ABCC2) as PXR-responsive with up to 19× induction; (v) LINCS L1000 rifampicin signature strength across 18 cell lines (HEPG2 ranks #1); and (vi) Open Targets disease-association graph (top genes recover textbook PXR pharmacology).

Contents: Python source (src/pxr_uncoupling/), entry-point scripts (scripts/), Jupyter notebooks (notebooks/), all processed CSVs (data/processed/), curated PXR target and negative-control gene tables (data/targets/), all rendered figures (figures/), manuscript (manuscript/manuscript.md), pinned environment (pyproject.toml, uv.lock), CI configuration (.github/workflows/), and 16 passing pytest unit tests (tests/).

Note: The raw CELLxGENE Census H5AD (data/raw/nr1i2_atlas.h5ad, ~600 MB) is not included in this Zenodo deposit; it can be reproduced from CELLxGENE Census v2025-01-30 by running gh workflow run fetch_atlas.yml on the GitHub repository. All downstream analyses run from cached CSVs without re-fetching the atlas.
